FIXED (2026-09-23, the gap X5 disclosed): a frame whose FIRST block is a compaction, an mcp_tool_result or a default content.block never had the replay-side bag applied (compaction/content.block blocks have no providerMetadata slot, and an mcp_tool_result's tool.done belongs to the adopted `<id>:result` message), so those wrapper facts were silently dropped. emitAssistantBlock now reports which halves anchored, and every UNANCHORED half rides the assistant message's message.metadata in wire order (the host half after a tool call, both halves after those three). INV-TURN (sp-protocol ruling B, 2026-09-23; ships in the 0.7.0 cohort, consumer-visible): turnIds are minted PER TURN, no longer per session. Through 0.6.4 every top-level turn was `turn_${session_id}` (so in a multi-turn invoke the second turn's message.start and content landed on T AFTER turn.done(T), with no second turn.start because the assembler's seen-turn set suppressed it, and reduce() merged the session's turns into one AgTurnRecord, and a resume, which keeps session_id unless forkSession is set (sdk.d.ts:1637-1641), collided across invokes). A top-level turn is now `turn_` + the id of the frame that opens it: the first assistant message id (complete frame or stream message_start), or the frame uuid when a notice or a result-only turn opens it; its result frame (either arm) closes and clears it. A closed id is never reopened (a late frame reusing a closed turn's message id opens under its own frame uuid), and a missing or non-string id/uuid falls back to a positional `turn_frame_<n>`. A nested turn is one per subagent RUN: `turn_` + the run's first nested message id, keyed by parent_tool_use_id (it was `turn_${session_id}` too); nested frames never open or name a top-level turn. A NESTED API-error frame never closes the parent (sp-protocol ruling 1, 2026-09-23; SPEC:97, INV-OWNER SPEC:753): the parent closes as an error only when its OWN result says so, and the nested failure rides a NON-terminal `error` event (SPEC:609) on the nested turn, inside the run's bracket. Through 0.6.4 (whenever subagent frames carried the parent's session_id) a nested rate_limit closed a recovered parent as a retriable error and, first-error-wins, masked a later top-level billing_error. subagent.done carries no outcome (SPEC:648), so the nested failure is live-only until sp-protocol bars that gap. ONE subagent BRACKET PER RUN (sp-protocol ruling, 2026-09-23; SPEC:807): the run opens once at its first nested frame and closes exactly once at whichever comes first, the spawning Task's tool_result (any user frame), the turn's result frame, or flush (at the result and at flush, innermost first; several Task results in one user frame close in content order); through the B commit it was per MESSAGE (N start/done pairs on one id). A nested frame for a CLOSED run (assistant, stream or tool_result, e.g. a background agent's after the parent's result) opens a new nested turn; a run that NEVER opened keeps Task 8c leg 3's synthetic label (parks loudly). Parallel Task calls give overlapping runs and the assembler's last-turn backfill is a LIFO stack, so top-level tool.done carries the open turn's id explicitly and a retraction's message.remove names the removed message's own turn; tool.args.* / ext.* carry no turnId, and a top-level tool.done with no turn open still backfills (pre-existing). No golden moves: the deferred message seal already placed a one-message run's subagent.done where the run close now lands. DISCLOSED, accepted by sp-protocol for its INV-FLUSH bar (wf_2231e194-e31): a notice after a session's last result opens a turn that INV-FLUSH aborts (stream-truncated) if nothing follows. threadId is unchanged (options.threadId ?? session_id). DRAFT.4 PHASE (rnd 13+17 stage 2, the claude leg of rd-13-17 A.6; SPEC §8.0 item 27, a SHOULD per the founder's A.10.5 ruling): a `thinking` block listed in the frame-local narration_block_indexes whose text is NON-EMPTY gets `phase:"interim"` on its reasoning block. On a complete-form frame it rides reasoning.start (known before the first delta). On a STREAMED frame, where the complete frame precedes the block's content_block_stop (CB-13; thinking-fable51 frames [62] signature, [63] frame, [64] stop), the listed frame-local index names stream block framedThrough + index (the blocks after those earlier frames covered); it is marked only while still open, and the phase rides its reasoning.end, only if its streamed text was non-empty. A frame naming an already-sealed block marks nothing, not a neighbour. A listed EMPTY block (display "omitted"; app-update-fable51's [4]) gets none, and a block that sealed before its frame arrived gets none (never a post-seal event). Never inferred from position, text or turn end; never decoded from the signature. The vendor list keeps riding host-only `_meta` verbatim (X5), and no committed golden moves. Zero live receipts: the only live narration frame is empty. KEEP (sp-protocol via sp-rnd, 2026-09-23): dormant on CLI 2.1.280, not wrong. Probe's live narration-opus55 (c805d20; opus-5-5, display 'summarized') shows 0 narration_block_indexes in 93 frames, and the steered progress updates arrive as unlisted text blocks; the only stamped cassette (app-update-fable51, display unset) lists an empty thinking block. Item 27 bars inferring phase from block position, text or turn end, so nothing else may stand in. Revisit when a CLI/SDK exposes display 'updates' or stamps a NON-EMPTY listed block. message.diagnostics (a Messages API response field; first live on sp-probe's defer-tool-sonnet5-resume-unavailable, 7c6880f: {cache_miss_reason: {type: 'tools_changed', cache_missed_input_tokens: 3258}}, the tool set changed between invokes) is CARRIED verbatim with its wire name on the first block's host-only _meta (the X5 route; response-only, so never providerMetadata per SPEC §12). Undeclared on @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.93.0's BetaMessage, so read through the JSON boundary; null/absent/non-object carries nothing. Per response, so once per SDK message id (again only when the value changes), not once per frame.

Both are outside C's no-text-inference basis, so the residual stands. isSynthetic (typed; first live on resume-unavailable, 7c6880f): a LIVE user frame with no tool_result block is content the CLI added itself (the host's own prompts come back only as isReplay acks), e.g. the isSynthetic nudge '[Your previous response had no visible output. …]' after an empty reply. Through ff87b81 it produced no event, and the census could not see its text drop (the path normalizes to the assistant text's). (2) DEFENSIVE, fixture-only (no 0.3.280 builder produces it): a replayed tool_result re-emitted tool.done; after its turn's turn.done that parked reduce() for the rest of the stream, the next turn included (INV-MSG, SPEC:745), and in a fresh or resumed normalizer it carried no turnId and parked from event 0. DISCLOSED GAP, pre-existing and unchanged: replayed string content that is the FIRST delivery (bash `<bash-input>` echo and output, local-command output, e.g. the model-switch notice) has no AgJSON event; candidate for the item-22 carry `ext.anthropic.frame{kind:'user'}` (an sp-protocol reading). The `tool_use_result` sibling was read on replays before the fix and is not now; only `file_attachments?` is unique to this arm, and it stays unread. SDKResultMessage.note: Union of SDKResultSuccess | SDKResultError. Success -> closeTurnDone (outcome/finishReason/usage/safety/permission_denials as denied tool.start+tool.done pairs). Every non-success subtype -> closeTurnError (errors joined, code=subtype, retriable = subtype !== 'error_max_turns'). FIELD-LEVEL DELTAS at 0.3.207 (name-only ratchet cannot see these; recorded from the full d.ts diff): (1) TerminalReason (`terminal_reason?:` on both result arms) widened by six values (api_error, malformed_tool_use_exhausted, budget_exhausted, structured_output_retry_exhausted, tool_deferred_unavailable, turn_setup_failed) — the facet reads `subtype`, never `terminal_reason`, so behavior is unchanged; the finer-grained reason is a disclosed unread field (candidate enrichment for turn.done/turn.error codes in a future slice). (2) `origin?:` — same SDKMessageOrigin delta as SDKUserMessage's disclosure. 0.3.217 bump audit: SDKResultSuccess additionally gains user_message_uuid?: string (correlation to the triggering user message) and request_sent_wall_ms?: number — same unread-telemetry class as the ttft_* family; behavior unchanged. 0.3.220 bump audit (2026-07-29), CARRIED: (1) fast_mode_disabled_reason?: FastModeDisabledReason lands on BOTH arms (why fast mode was blocked — 'free'|'preference'|'extra_usage_disabled'|'network_error'|'unknown'|'not_first_party'|'disabled_by_env'|'model_not_allowed'|'sdk_opt_in_required'|'pending'); (2) ModelUsage (the modelUsage record's values, also both arms) gains canonicalModel?: string (the pricing-lookup id behind a provider-specific/alias key) and provider?: string ('firstParty'|'bedrock'|'vertex'|... — typed open string) — added for billing rate-table selection. Neither has a core home: turn.done/turn.error carry no providerMetadata slot and AgUsage is a closed schema (a byModel entry cannot carry identity fields) — both ride ONE structured ext event `ext.anthropic.result-meta` {fastModeDisabledReason?, modelUsage?: {<model>: {canonicalModel?, provider?}}} emitted immediately before the turn close (the ext.anthropic.informational structured-carry precedent, fields camelCased); absent fields emit nothing (pre-0.3.220 output byte-identical). A first-class turn-close providerMetadata slot / AgUsage identity slot is a future spec-process decision, disclosed rather than forced. VALUE-LEVEL at 0.3.220: api_error_status now populates 429/529 where it was previously null — the facet never reads it; unread-telemetry class, disposition unchanged. 0.3.258 bump (2026-09-02): ModelUsage gains costBasis ('list'|'managed'|'unknown', 0.3.246) and thinkingTokens (0.3.257, a SUBSET of outputTokens); both result arms gain queued_turn_count (0 is real) and SDKResultError gains user_message_uuid. costBasis joins the per-model identity in ext.anthropic.result-meta.modelUsage[model]; userMessageUuid + queuedTurnCount ride result-meta top-level; thinkingTokens → usage.byModel[model].reasoningTokens and usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens (runtime-guarded; undeclared on the resolved BetaUsage 0.93.0) → usage.reasoningTokens. RUNTIME-ONLY subagent_stats (undeclared; on every 0.3.258 result) is carried WHOLE as result-meta.subagentStats. Cost semantics: costUsd now follows Claude Code's pricing basis (0.3.239 US-inference 1.1x, 0.3.246 managed rates) — costBasis tells consumers which table applied. Live 2.1.258 price table still says maxOutputTokens 64000 for sonnet-5/fable-5-1 vs the Models API's 128000 — a CLI-table artefact, carried verbatim. 0.3.261 bump (2026-09-05): BOTH arms gain user_message_uuids?: string[] (0.3.259) — the first-frame list plus 'any queued user message folded into the running turn between tool rounds, once taken off the queue', so the result copy can be LONGER than the reply frame's copy (both copies are carried; neither is redundant). CARRIED as result-meta.userMessageUuids beside userMessageUuid (camelCase per the result-meta convention; Array.isArray + every-string guard, verbatim, invariants not validated). SDKResultSuccess additionally gains four bare remote-session latency fields first_content_frame_ms / first_stream_post_ms / first_stream_post_ack_ms / first_stream_post_wall_ms (0.3.260, NOT on SDKResultError) — ROUTER-PLANE, the same unread wall-clock class as ttft_ms/ttft_stream_ms/time_to_request_ms; allowlisted reviewed:any claude-scoped proactively (local-CLI captures are not expected to emit them). Neither member of the user_message_uuid family has ever appeared in a cassette (string-prompt capture path) — see SDKAssistantMessage. cohort 0.6.3 (CL-09 fix, live-confirmed): a success result with is_error:true is an API-error turn. If a TOP-LEVEL assistant `error` frame preceded it, this result - on EITHER result arm, whatever is_error says - emits that frame's stashed turn.error exactly once (a NESTED error frame never stashes: sp-protocol ruling 1, see SDKAssistantMessage), carrying this result's usage; the first error frame wins; with no result at all, flush emits the stashed close without usage and never an engine turn.abort. With no preceding error frame (0.6.2 closed this as turn.done{success}) it closes as turn.error {message: result, code: api_error_code ?? 'api_error', retriable: api_error_status 429 or >= 500, usage}. Denials ride the ordinary <turnId>:denials carrier (the turn is still open at the result frame), ahead of result-meta and the close, as on every turn. result-meta gains apiErrorCode (undeclared api_error_code, success arm) and startupFailureReason (SDKResultError.startup_failure_reason, 0.3.274); a present startupFailureReason makes retriable false except worktree_unverified, the only value upstream calls retriable. 0.3.277 BEHAVIOUR CHANGE on carried values: total_cost_usd and modelUsage now continue across resume and fork (from the total the transcript saved, when it has one), so on a resumed stream the first turn.done's usage.costUsd and usage.byModel include spend from earlier process lifetimes; no wire field marks it and the spec forbids normalizer subtraction, so it is recorded here, not corrected. KNOWN GAP (pre-existing): denials declared on an error-subtype result are not emitted. ERROR-ARM DENIALS (2026-09-23, seat queue item 1): SDKResultError declares permission_denials too (e.g. error_max_turns after a denied tool), but through 0.6.4 only the success arm emitted the `<turnId>:denials` carrier, so an error-subtype result dropped its denials. Both arms now share one carrier (`emitDenialsCarrier`) at the same point: after the seal and the run closes, before result-meta and the close. On the error arm the array is shape-guarded (discriminant-validated arm), and a malformed entry is skipped. Fixture-only: no seed has an error-subtype result with denials. RESULT-FRAME TRIAGE (2026-09-23, seat queue item 3; 0.3.280 d.ts vs registry/allowlist/manifest): SDKResultSuccess declares eight fields that were never observed, registered or noted. SEVEN are router-plane latency telemetry, bare and undocumented, the same family as the allowlisted ttft_ms / time_to_request_ms / first_stream_post_{ms,ack_ms,wall_ms}: first_stream_post_queue_wait_ms, first_stream_post_queued_behind ('durable_post'|'ephemeral_post'|'retry_backoff'|'hold'|'none'; 0.3.280), first_text_post_ms, first_text_post_wall_ms, time_to_request_from_spawn_ms, warm_spare_claimed and time_origin_ms. They have no AgJSON home, are never read, and belong on the allowlist as reviewed:any when a capture shows them (sp-probe's registry; request_sent_wall_ms joins that class from the multi-result capture). The EIGHTH, deferred_tool_use (SDKDeferredToolUse {id, name, input}), is CONTENT: the tool call a host's PreToolUse `defer` decision parked, which the CLI resumes later. Through 0.6.4 it was dropped. It is now CARRIED whole and verbatim as ext.anthropic.result-meta.deferredToolUse (the subagentStats precedent). Whether it should map onto turn.done.outcome.paused (asks) instead is routed to sp-protocol / sp-rnd. Fixture-only: no capture sets a defer hook. RESULT-META ERROR CARRIES (2026-09-23; sp-probe's api-error-auth seed, the first live is_error:true cassette): api_error_status, read before only for retriable, now also rides ext.anthropic.result-meta.apiErrorStatus verbatim (number; absent/null gives no key), beside apiErrorCode. The result's stop_reason, on a result that closes as turn.error (the error arm, a stashed CL-09 close, or is_error:true), rides result-meta.stopReason verbatim, because turn.error has no finishReason slot and finishReasonRaw is turn.done-only. A success close keeps it on finishReason alone, so ordinary goldens do not move. The census's stop_reason transform takes the ANY-OF target [finishReason, stopReason] (sp-probe 7322f73). 0.7.0 (D, sp-protocol conformance 2026-09-23): the permission_denials carrier skips every entry whose tool_use_id already has its final tool.done in this invoke (a tool_result, an mcp_tool_result, or an earlier carrier, so a repeated id gets one pair); an id not yet closed still gets its tool.start+tool.done{denied} pair, and no carrier message opens when none remain. Before this, a hook-blocked call closed 'error' at its tool_result and then again 'denied' from the aggregate: a duplicate tool.start and a second final tool.done (rd-14 P14 parks it). The CLI dedupes permission_denials by id and collects them per engine turn (2.1.280 binary).
